newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotels shareholder sues Donald Trump.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotels shareholder sues Donald Trump.

text.p: A shareholder of Trump Hotels and Casino Resorts Inc has sued Donald Trump, the Trump casino organization and Salomon Brothers Inc in an action related to Trump Hotels' recent acquisition of a Atlantic City, N.J., resort.
The shareholder, Richard Ziemak, alleges that Donald Trump inflated the price of his Trump Castle Hotel & Casino Resort by as much as $100 million before selling it to Trump Hotels last month.
Donald Trump is also Trump Hotels' chairman and its largest single stockholder. Salomon advised Trump Hotels on the transaction.
The eight-count complaint, filed on Wednesday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, alleges that Donald Trump breached his fiduciary duty to Trump Hotels.
It also alleges violations of proxy Rule 14a-9 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 in proxy materials filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to gain approval of the acquisition.
On September 30, Trump Hotels shareholders approved the $480 million acquisition of the Trump Castle from Donald Trump.
But according to the court filing, the total reported value of the transaction, including the assumption of debt, was $525 million.
The law firm representing Ziemak -- Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP -- was unavailable for comment.
To facilitate the acquisition, Donald Trump co-opted and conspired with other members of Trump Hotels' board, Salomon and other defendants named in the action, the suit alleges.

The lawsuit also alleges Salomon breached its disclosure obligations in its opinion on the fairness of the acquisition price to a committee of Trump Hotels' independent directors. The firm presented its opinion on June 24.
According to the court papers, Salomon was paid $2.6 million to review the transaction and issue its fairness opinion.
Salomon officials could not be reached for comment late Friday.
